content.text:
Here is how owner "address" is currently handled across the repository at /home/daniel/sandbox.

## Summary / key finding

There is **no separate hand-written Owner request/DTO class**. The request and response DTOs (`OwnerFieldsDto`, `OwnerDto`, `OwnerPageDto`) are **generated at build time from the OpenAPI spec** `src/main/resources/openapi.yml` (they do not exist as `.java` files in the tree). Address today is a single flat `address` string. The acceptance test already references a not-yet-implemented **structured address** (`addressLine1`/`addressLine2`) feature — `grep` confirms `addressLine` does not appear anywhere in `src/main`.

---

## 1. Owner request/DTO with the "address" field (source of truth: OpenAPI)

`src/main/resources/openapi.yml` — schema `OwnerFields` (lines 1991-2081) is the create/update request body; `Owner` (lines 2082-2267) is the response. Relevant `address`/`postcode` fragments:

```yaml
OwnerFields:            # lines 1991-2081
  properties:
    address:
      title: Address
      description: The postal address of the pet owner.
      type: string
      minLength: 1
      maxLength: 255
      example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
    ...
    postcode:
      description: >-
        The 4-digit postal code ... must be valid for the city's region using the fixed
        city-to-region table (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099); a city with
        no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode.
      type: string
      pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
      example: '2000'
  required: [firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone]
```

Response-only `Owner` adds `locality`, `timezone`, `customerCode`, `householdId`, etc. (lines 2117-2171), all `readOnly`.

The generated `OwnerFieldsDto` is what every owner function operates on (validation, normalization all mutate this DTO). Its bean-validation constraints (`minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`) come from the YAML above and are enforced via `@Valid` in `ValidateOwner`.

---

## 2. Address normalization, household hash, postcode validation, locality

### AddressNormalizer — `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/AddressNormalizer.java`
Package-private helper. Trims, collapses inner whitespace, upper-cases, expands street abbreviations (`ST->STREET`, `RD->ROAD`, `AVE->AVENUE`). `null`/all-whitespace normalizes to `""`.

```java
private static final Map<String, String> ABBREVIATIONS = Map.of("ST","STREET","RD","ROAD","AVE","AVENUE");
static String normalize(String address) {
    if (address == null) return "";
    String collapsed = address.strip().replaceAll("\\s+", " ").toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
    if (collapsed.isEmpty()) return "";
    String[] tokens = collapsed.split(" ");
    ... // rebuilds, replacing each token via ABBREVIATIONS.getOrDefault
}
```

### NormalizeOwnerAddress — `.../owner/NormalizeOwnerAddress.java`
OfficeFloor function that applies `AddressNormalizer.normalize` in place on the request DTO.
```java
public void service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request) {
    request.setAddress(AddressNormalizer.normalize(request.getAddress()));
}
```

### Household (household hash) — `.../owner/Household.java`
Household id = first **12 hex chars** of `SHA-256(normalizedLastName + '|' + postcode)`. Returns `null` when no postcode.
```java
private static final int ID_LENGTH = 12;
static String normalizeLastName(String lastName) {
    return lastName == null ? "" : lastName.strip().replaceAll("\\s+", " ").toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
}
static String idFor(String lastName, String postcode) {
    if (!StringUtils.hasText(postcode)) return null;
    return Sha256.hex(normalizeLastName(lastName) + '|' + postcode).substring(0, ID_LENGTH);
}
```
Note: `Household` uses last name + postcode only; it does **not** currently incorporate the address string.

### Sha256 — `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Sha256.java`
`Sha256.hex(value)` → full upper-case hex SHA-256 (UTF-8). Shared by customer code and household id.

### ValidateOwnerPostcode — `.../owner/ValidateOwnerPostcode.java`
Optional postcode; if present must be 4 digits and in range for the city's region, else `InvalidPostcodeException` (400).
```java
private static final Pattern FOUR_DIGITS = Pattern.compile("[0-9]{4}");
public void service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request) throws InvalidPostcodeException {
    String postcode = request.getPostcode();
    if (!StringUtils.hasText(postcode)) return;
    if (!FOUR_DIGITS.matcher(postcode).matches()
            || !RegionPostcodes.isInRange(CityRegion.of(request.getCity()), Integer.parseInt(postcode)))
        throw new InvalidPostcodeException(postcode, request.getCity());
}
```

### Locality lookups (models)
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/CityRegion.java` — fixed city→region map (Sydney→NSW, Melbourne→VIC, Brisbane→QLD), default `UNKNOWN`.
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/RegionPostcodes.java` — region→postcode range (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099); `isInRange(region, postcode)` and `regionOf(postcode)`.
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/CustomerCode.java` — `<REGION>-<HASH8>`; `regionOf(customerCode)` returns the REGION portion, which is what `Owner.getLocality()` returns.
- Locality itself is computed on the entity: `Owner.getLocality()` = `CustomerCode.regionOf(this.customerCode)` (Owner.java lines 230-233).

---

## 3. Owner entity and response mapping

### Entity — `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`
Flat `address` field (lines 38-40), plus `city`, `telephone`, `email`, `postcode`, `householdId`, `customerCode`, etc.
```java
@Column(name = "address")
@NotEmpty
private String address;   // getAddress/setAddress at lines 90-96
```
Derived transients: `getLocality()` (230-233), `getTimezone()` (240-243), `getIdentityKey()` (289-292). `toString()` includes `address` (line 366). Note `address` is the only address-related column; no `addressLine1/2`.

### Mapper — `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java`
MapStruct interface: `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)`, `toOwnerDto(Owner)` (+`displayName` expression), `toOwnerDto(Owner, boolean bulkSignupWarning)`, `toOwnerPageDto(Page<Owner>)`. Address maps by name (no custom mapping), so any new address fields must be added to both entity and DTO or given explicit `@Mapping`.

### Response functions
- `.../owner/RespondWithOwner.java` — GET single (200).
- `.../owner/RespondWithOwnerCreated.java` — POST (201 + Location).
- `.../owner/RespondWithOwnerUpdated.java` — PUT (204).

---

## 4. Tests relating to owner address / validation / household / postcode / locality / normalization

Only acceptance-level tests exist (no unit tests for the owner functions). All under `src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/`.

### `AcceptanceTest.java` (whole file, 27 lines) — the structured-address checkpoint (currently the target feature)
```java
/** address-structured: structured addressLine1/city/postcode is accepted and normalized (
 * rules: upper-case, collapse whitespace, expand ST->STREET), and 'address' is the composed

            returned when given.

                QLD->Australia/Brisbane). Absent when the locality has no known timezone.

              readOnly: true

      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. Accepted in national or international form
            (spaces, dashes and brackets are ignored); stored and returned in E.164 form,
            assuming country code +61 when none is supplied.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; stored lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The 4-digit postal code of the pet owner. Optional. When supplied it must be valid for
            the city's region using the fixed city-to-region table (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099,
            QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and
            returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. Optional; defaults to the server's current date when not supplied.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The pet owner's date of birth. Optional; when supplied it is used to derive the
            owner's age band (see 'ageBand') as of the registration date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Request-only opt-in acknowledging that this owner deliberately shares a household with an
            existing owner. When true, the create endpoint skips the duplicate-household rejection that
            fires when another owner already has the same last name and postcode, and the owner is
            created as a declared household member rather than being flagged a possible duplicate.
          type: boolean
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-
                The stored E.164 telephone formatted for humans: the country code, a space, then the
                national digits grouped in threes. The raw 'telephone' stays in E.164 form.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of the first and last name, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The owner's locality: the REGION portion of its customerCode, i.e. the region derived from
                the postcode (falling back to the city), or 'UNKNOWN' when neither resolves to a region.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            timezone:
              title: Timezone
              description: >-
                The owner's IANA timezone, derived from its locality (region) via the fixed
                region-to-timezone table (NSW->Australia/Sydney, VIC->Australia/Melbourne,
                QLD->Australia/Brisbane). Absent when the locality has no known timezone.
              type: string
              example: 'Australia/Sydney'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code formatted '<REGION>-<HASH8>', where REGION is the region code
                derived from the postcode (falling back to the city, else 'UNKNOWN') and HASH8 is the first
                8 upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over the normalized telephone followed by the last
                name.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>', where YY is the last two
                digits of the registration date year.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                The single Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits of the customerCode,
                guarding against transcription errors of the code.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                Deterministic identifier of the owner's household: the first 12 hex characters of
                SHA-256 over the normalized last name and the postcode, so owners with the same last
                name and postcode share it automatically. Absent for an owner without a postcode.
              type: string
              example: '1A2B3C4D5E6F'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners that shared this owner's first and last name
                (case-insensitively) at the moment it was created.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                The owner's membership points, assigned on creation. Starting from 0, points accrue
                for each loyalty factor: +2 for an email address, +1 for no namesakes at creation
                (namesakeCount is 0), +2 for a household of 3 or more, and +3 for a tenure of more
                than 365 days. A newly created owner has zero tenure, so at creation the total
                cannot exceed 5.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level, derived from its membershipPoints: 1 for
                0-1 points, 2 for 2-3, 3 for 4-5 and 4 for 6 or more. A newly created owner has zero
                tenure, so at creation the level cannot exceed 3; level 4 requires accrued tenure.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: >-
                True when more than 80 owners have already been registered on the current date,
                signalling an unusually high sign-up volume; false otherwise.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: >-
                The owner's preferred contact channel, derived from the stored details:
                'EMAIL' when an email address is present, otherwise 'PHONE'.
              type: string
              example: 'PHONE'
              readOnly: true
            ageBand:
              title: Age band
              description: >-
                The owner's age band derived from the birth date against the registration date:
                'MINOR' (under 18), 'ADULT' (18-64) or 'SENIOR' (65+). Absent when no birth date
                was supplied.
              type: string
              example: 'ADULT'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The single derived key all duplicate detection is expressed through, formed as
                '<normalizedTelephone>|<email or empty>|<householdId or empty>'. Two owners collide
                only when their whole identity keys are equal.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678||1A2B3C4D5E6F'
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicate:
              title: Possible duplicate
              description: >-
                True when, at creation, an existing owner shared this owner's household (same last
                name and postcode) but was reachable on a different telephone (a soft match that is
                still created). A declared household member (opted in via 'sharesHousehold') is never
                flagged. False otherwise.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicateOf:
              title: Possible duplicate of
              description: >-
                The id of the existing owner this one was flagged a possible duplicate of at creation
                (see 'possibleDuplicate'). Absent when not flagged.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the pet owner's structured postal address. Preferred over the flat
            'address' when supplied. Stored and returned normalized (upper-cased, whitespace
            collapsed, street-type abbreviations expanded).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the pet owner's structured postal address. Stored and
            returned normalized, and appended to 'addressLine1' (single space) to form 'address'.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 5'
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted as flat input for backward compatibility
            when no structured 'addressLine1' is supplied. Always returned as the composed,
            normalized address: 'addressLine1' with the normalized 'addressLine2' appended after a
            single space when present, otherwise the normalized flat address.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. Accepted in national or international form
            (spaces, dashes and brackets are ignored); stored and returned in E.164 form,
            assuming country code +61 when none is supplied.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; stored lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The 4-digit postal code of the pet owner. Optional. When supplied it must be valid for
            the city's region using the fixed city-to-region table (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099,
            QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and
            returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. Optional; defaults to the server's current date when not supplied.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The pet owner's date of birth. Optional; when supplied it is used to derive the
            owner's age band (see 'ageBand') as of the registration date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Request-only opt-in acknowledging that this owner deliberately shares a household with an
            existing owner. When true, the create endpoint skips the duplicate-household rejection that
            fires when another owner already has the same last name and postcode, and the owner is
            created as a declared household member rather than being flagged a possible duplicate.
          type: boolean
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-
                The stored E.164 telephone formatted for humans: the country code, a space, then the
                national digits grouped in threes. The raw 'telephone' stays in E.164 form.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of the first and last name, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The owner's locality: the REGION portion of its customerCode, i.e. the region derived from
                the postcode (falling back to the city), or 'UNKNOWN' when neither resolves to a region.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            timezone:
              title: Timezone
              description: >-
                The owner's IANA timezone, derived from its locality (region) via the fixed
                region-to-timezone table (NSW->Australia/Sydney, VIC->Australia/Melbourne,
                QLD->Australia/Brisbane). Absent when the locality has no known timezone.
              type: string
              example: 'Australia/Sydney'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code formatted '<REGION>-<HASH8>', where REGION is the region code
                derived from the postcode (falling back to the city, else 'UNKNOWN') and HASH8 is the first
                8 upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over the normalized telephone followed by the last
                name.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>', where YY is the last two
                digits of the registration date year.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                The single Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits of the customerCode,
                guarding against transcription errors of the code.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                Deterministic identifier of the owner's household: the first 12 hex characters of
                SHA-256 over the normalized last name and the postcode, so owners with the same last
                name and postcode share it automatically. Absent for an owner without a postcode.
              type: string
              example: '1A2B3C4D5E6F'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners that shared this owner's first and last name
                (case-insensitively) at the moment it was created.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                The owner's membership points, assigned on creation. Starting from 0, points accrue
                for each loyalty factor: +2 for an email address, +1 for no namesakes at creation
                (namesakeCount is 0), +2 for a household of 3 or more, and +3 for a tenure of more
                than 365 days. A newly created owner has zero tenure, so at creation the total
                cannot exceed 5.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level, derived from its membershipPoints: 1 for
                0-1 points, 2 for 2-3, 3 for 4-5 and 4 for 6 or more. A newly created owner has zero
                tenure, so at creation the level cannot exceed 3; level 4 requires accrued tenure.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: >-
                True when more than 80 owners have already been registered on the current date,
                signalling an unusually high sign-up volume; false otherwise.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: >-
                The owner's preferred contact channel, derived from the stored details:
                'EMAIL' when an email address is present, otherwise 'PHONE'.
              type: string
              example: 'PHONE'
              readOnly: true
            ageBand:
              title: Age band
              description: >-
                The owner's age band derived from the birth date against the registration date:
                'MINOR' (under 18), 'ADULT' (18-64) or 'SENIOR' (65+). Absent when no birth date

The design centres on one idea: **compute the effective, normalized address once and store it in the flat `address` field**, so every downstream step reads a single canonical value regardless of which form the request used.

**Contract (`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`)**

**Address logic (`AddressNormalizer.compose`)**
- New reusable method encapsulating the rule: prefer `addressLine1` (normalized) with normalized `addressLine2` appended after a single space when present; otherwise fall back to the normalized flat `address`; empty string when neither is supplied. Reuses the existing `normalize`.

**Wiring**
- `NormalizeOwnerAddress` now normalizes whichever fields are supplied and sets `address` to the composed value.
- `ValidateRequiredOwnerFields` checks the composed address, so a request is valid with a non-blank `addressLine1` **or** a flat `address` (plus city) — earlier minimal owners still accepted.
- For consistency, PUT now runs the same `NormalizeOwnerAddress` step and `ApplyOwner` copies the structured fields — so updates behave identically to creates.

Because `city`/`postcode` are shared top-level fields and the composed value is stored in `address`, the household hash (lastName + postcode), postcode validation and locality all naturally read the effective address without further change.
